I've been working this land for 36 years. I know Quzhou's soil — alkaline, sandy-loamy, and the summers are hot and dry. I have my well, and I know how to use it. My body is getting older, just two of us now, so I have to be careful not to take on more than we can manage.

My 15 mu breaks down like this: 10 mu for the wheat-maize rotation that I've always done, and 5 mu for cotton. Cotton is hard work but I've done it my whole life and I know how to manage it.

**Wheat (winter, 10 mu):** I'll plant an improved wheat variety — the kind from the county seed station, something like Jimai or Luyuan series. I know these perform well here. I apply base fertilizer before plowing, then topdress at jointing. I water four times: the winter water to protect roots from freezing, the green-up water in spring, jointing water, and grain-filling water. I spray twice — once for weeds early, once for aphids and rust near heading. I use rotary tillage before planting to break up the maize stubble.

**Maize (summer, 10 mu):** Right after wheat harvest in June, I plant hybrid maize seed. I do no-till direct seeding — saves time and the soil is warm and ready. I fertilize at planting and again when plants are knee-high. I only water if it's dry at planting, then again at tasseling and grain fill. Two pesticide passes — herbicide first, then one for stem borers.

**Cotton (spring, 5 mu):** I plant cotton in late April. It needs the most work — I know this. I use an improved cotton variety. Heavy pest pressure every year: aphids, bollworm, red spider mites. I'll spray 8 times through the season. Four waterings. I plough this field deeply before planting to break up the hard pan.
